name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
authors: Aman Madaan, Niket Tandon, Prakhar Gupta, et al. (16+ authors); lead affiliation Carnegie Mellon University (LTI), with Allen Institute for AI (AI2), University of Washington, NVIDIA, UC San Diego, Google Research/Brain Team.
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Neural Information Processing Systems); arXiv preprint 2303.17651.
code_url: https://selfrefine.info/ (code, data, and prompts; project page links GitHub release).
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique. A single frozen LLM acts as generator, feedback provider, and refiner; the feedback step is the model verbally critiquing its own output in natural language.
feedback_source: self-generated. The same LLM produces natural-language, multi-aspect, actionable feedback on its own output via a few-shot feedback prompt; no external tool, unit test, reward, or human is used in the core method (an external incorrect-answer signal is only explored as an ablation for Math Reasoning in Appendix H.1).
iteration_structure: iterative-refine. Alternates feedback->refine on the same draft for a fixed max of 4 iterations or until the model/task-specific stopping criterion signals no further refinement is needed.
reflection_object: output content. The method reflects on and rewrites the previously generated output (dialogue response, code, sentence, math solution, acronym), not the action trajectory or model weights. Feedback is multi-aspect natural language tied to the specific output; prompts are fixed and not modified across iterations.
requires_training: none. Training-free / test-time only; no supervised training data, no fine-tuning, no reinforcement learning. Relies solely on few-shot prompting of a frozen LLM.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge. The same generator LLM serves as its own critic/feedback provider; there is no trained reward model, no separate critic, and no verifiable reward in the core method.
distillation_target: none. Reflection is consumed within the single task episode to refine the current output; it is not distilled into any persisted reusable artifact (no memory, skill library, or weight update).
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered. The reflective behavior is prompt/scaffold-engineered: three hand-written few-shot prompts (initial generation, feedback, refine) elicit and incorporate self-feedback. It is not an RL-emergent capability.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad. The running output plus accumulated feedback history is appended into the prompt context within the episode; there is no long-term or cross-episode memory store.
memory_persistence: within-episode. Feedback and refined drafts persist only within the single task instance's feedback-refine loop and do not transfer across tasks or sessions.
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only. Prior feedback and outputs are appended to the history given to the refine step (the paper notes retaining the full feedback/output history helps the model avoid repeating mistakes); there is no summarization, Pareto selection, or eviction.
error_localization_granularity: response-level. Feedback is generated on the whole output and is multi-aspect/actionable (e.g., pointing at a specific inefficiency in code or an unaddressed concept), but localization is at the level of the output as a whole rather than formal step-level/token-level attribution. The paper explicitly notes that in Math Reasoning the model often fails to localize the single erroneous line/operation, limiting gains.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task. Refines within a single task instance using self-feedback; it does not transfer experience across tasks or episodes (contrast with Reflexion/ExpeL).
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision. Operates after an output is produced, revising the completed draft via feedback; it does not recover mid-trajectory during action execution nor retry across fresh episodes.
task_domains: Natural-language generation and source-code generation/reasoning: dialogue response generation, code optimization, code readability improvement, math reasoning, sentiment reversal (controllable generation), acronym generation, and constrained generation.
benchmarks: Dialogue Response Generation (FED; Mehri & Eskenazi 2020), Code Optimization (PIE; Madaan et al. 2023), Code Readability Improvement (CodeNet; Puri et al. 2021), Math Reasoning (GSM8K; Cobbe et al. 2021), Sentiment Reversal (Yelp; Zhang et al. 2015), Acronym Generation (new task), and Constrained Generation (CommonGen-Hard, a harder 20-30 keyword variant of CommonGen; Lin et al. 2020).
headline_result: Across 7 tasks, Self-Refine improves over the same base LLM's one-step generation by ~20% absolute on average (range 5-40% absolute). With GPT-4: Constrained Generation 15.0->45.0 (+30.0), Dialogue Response (GPT-4 pref) 25.4->74.6 (+49.2), Sentiment Reversal 3.8->36.2 (+32.4), Code Optimization 27.3->36.0 (+8.7); with ChatGPT Code Readability 27.7->63.1 (+35.4). Math Reasoning (GSM8K) is essentially flat (GPT-4 92.9->93.1, +0.2).
baselines: The same base LLMs without feedback-refine iterations: GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003), ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo), GPT-4, and Codex (code-davinci-002) for code tasks. Also compared against prior state-of-the-art and additional few-shot/fine-tuned approaches (Appendix F), and against generic-feedback / no-feedback ablations.
gains_vs_baseline: Versus the same base model (the strongest comparable baseline), GPT-4+Self-Refine deltas: Sentiment Reversal +32.4, Dialogue Response +49.2, Code Optimization +8.7, Code Readability +28.8, Math Reasoning +0.2, Acronym Generation +25.6, Constrained Generation +30.0. ChatGPT and GPT-3.5 show similar consistent (mostly positive) gains; gains are largest on preference-based and constrained-generation tasks and negligible on GSM8K math.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-only multiplier: each task instance costs roughly (1 + 2k) LLM calls for k feedback-refine iterations (1 initial generation + a feedback call and a refine call per iteration), with a max of 4 iterations (so up to ~9 calls/instance). No training/gradient cost. Most quality gains accrue in the first 1-2 iterations (diminishing returns), e.g., Constrained Gen 29.0->40.3->46.7->49.7 across y0..y3.
known_limitations: (1) Requires base models with strong few-shot/instruction-following ability; weaker open models may not benefit. (2) Experiments use only closed models (GPT-3.5/ChatGPT/GPT-4/Codex) whose details are undisclosed and which are not free. (3) English-only datasets; benefits may not transfer to other languages. (4) Could be misused to steer models toward toxic/harmful text; no explicit guard. (5) Weak on Math Reasoning because the model often cannot detect whether an error exists (e.g., ChatGPT feedback says 'everything looks good' for 94% of instances), revealing dependence on the model's ability to verify its own correctness.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only (self-verify) in the core method: feedback is purely self-generated with no oracle label or external verifier. However, the paper itself shows Math Reasoning gains jump to 5%+ only when an external source can flag whether the current answer is incorrect (Appendix H.1), and follow-up critiques (Huang et al. 2023) report that on reasoning the intrinsic-only improvements vanish without oracle labels. So intrinsic-only is reliable mainly on open-ended/preference tasks, not on verifiable reasoning.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent. Net-positive and large on open-ended generation, controllable generation, and constrained generation; near-zero on math reasoning. Subsequent analysis (Huang et al. 2023, 'LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet') argues intrinsic self-correction on reasoning is net-negative/non-improving once oracle stopping labels are removed, framing Self-Refine's reasoning gains as partly dependent on external feedback or favorable task structure.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper does not report calibration / confidence metrics; the 'reasoning tax' / overconfidence lens predates the reasoning-model literature and is not analyzed for Self-Refine. (Relatedly, the paper notes the model is poorly calibrated at error detection in math, e.g., declaring 'everything looks good' on 94% of GSM8K instances.)
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. Self-Refine is a self-refinement method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it does not classify failure modes, attribute responsible agents, or do counterfactual error localization (its feedback is corrective rather than diagnostic over a multi-agent trace).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets first-pass output deficiencies: incomplete coverage of constraints (missing concepts in constrained generation), suboptimal/inefficient code, poor readability, unengaging or low-user-understanding dialogue, and wrong sentiment/style. In MAST terms it is closest to mitigating 'superficial' single-shot output errors; it conversely exhibits the 'superficial self-reflection' / under-detection failure on math where the critic cannot find the error.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Introduces two new tasks/datasets - Acronym Generation and Constrained Generation (CommonGen-Hard, a harder 20-30 keyword variant of CommonGen) - and releases all code, prompts, and model outputs at https://selfrefine.info/. No multi-agent failure-trace corpus.
builds_on: Iterative-refinement and self-critique work without supervised refiners: human iterative-refinement framing (Simon 1962; Flower & Hayes 1981); few-shot/in-context prompting (Brown et al. 2020 GPT-3); learned/prompted refiners it contrasts with (PEER Schick et al. 2022, Self-Critique Saunders et al. 2022, Self-Correction Welleck et al. 2022, CodeRL Le et al. 2022, Re3 Yang et al. 2022, Augmenter/LLM-Augmenter Peng et al. 2023); contemporaneous self-reflection prompting (Reflexion Shinn et al. 2023). It positions itself as supervision-free, multi-aspect, iterative self-feedback within a single LLM.
extended_by_or_inspired: Widely cited as the canonical training-free intrinsic self-refinement baseline. Inspired/contrasted by: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) verbal RL with episodic memory; CRITIC (Gou et al. 2023) tool-verified self-correction; Self-Debugging (Chen et al. 2023); RCI (Kim et al. 2023); multi-agent debate (Du et al. 2023). Critically examined by 'Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet' (Huang et al. 2023, ICLR 2024) and survey/critique work (Pan et al. 2023; Kamoi et al. 2024 'When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes?'). Also a baseline for later refinement frameworks like Self-Refine-style metacognitive systems (e.g., Monitor-Generate-Verify, 2025).
citation_count: ~3638 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026); among the most-cited training-free self-refinement papers.
reasoning_model_native: no. Predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; it is a prompt-engineered scaffold over GPT-3.5/GPT-4-class models. Its weak math-reasoning results and the Huang et al. critique are often cited as motivation for RL-trained native reflection in later reasoning models.
on_policy_distillation_link: none / weak. Self-Refine performs no distillation and no weight updates, so it has no direct on-policy-distillation or skill-optimization mechanism; its self-generated feedback-refine traces are sometimes used by later work as data sources for distilling self-correction into weights, but that is external to this paper.
sample_efficiency: Reaches reported gains within a small number of iterations (max 4); most improvement is captured in the first 1-2 feedback-refine rounds with diminishing returns thereafter (e.g., Constrained Gen y0=29.0, y1=40.3, y2=46.7, y3=49.7; Code Opt y0=22.0 -> y3=28.8). No training trials required.
